clone.title: How Arc::clone works
clone.description: Shares ownership across threads by counting references atomically.

title.text: let a = Arc::new(vec![1, 2, 3]); let b = Arc::clone(&a);

slides.caption: Arc is like Rc, but its counter is updated atomically, so clones can move to other threads.
Arc::clone makes b, which can be moved into a thread: count 2.
Arc gives shared read access. To change the data too, wrap it: Arc<Mutex<T>>.

new.title: How Arc::new works
new.description: Puts a value on the heap so several threads can share it.

slides.caption: Arc works like Rc, but its counter is safe to update from many threads.
The Vec moves to the heap.
Clone the Arc for each thread; the data itself is not copied.

strong_count.title: How Arc::strong_count works
strong_count.description: How many Arc owners share the value.

slides.caption: Each Arc::clone adds one; each drop subtracts one.
main plus two clones for threads.
With threads running, the number can change at any moment; use it for debugging, not logic.

try_unwrap.title: How Arc::try_unwrap works
try_unwrap.description: Takes the value out if this is the only owner; otherwise gives the Arc back.

slides.caption: Once the threads have finished, the last owner can take the data back.
Another clone exists: Err, with the Arc returned.
Arc::into_inner is a simpler version that returns an Option.

make_mut.title: How Arc::make_mut works
make_mut.description: Mutable access, cloning the value first if others share it.

slides.caption: b still uses the old value, so a gets a private copy before changing.
Shared: the Vec is cloned for a.
a's copy changes; b is untouched.
If a was the only owner, no clone happens.

downgrade.title: How Arc::downgrade works
downgrade.description: Makes a thread-safe Weak pointer that does not keep the value alive.

slides.caption: The Weak can later upgrade() to an Arc if the value still exists.
Breaks reference cycles between threads' shared structures.

ptr_eq.title: How Arc::ptr_eq works
ptr_eq.description: true if two Arcs share the same allocation.

slides.caption: Equal contents are not enough: it must be the same block of memory.
A clone shares the allocation: true.
A new Arc with an equal value: false.

get_mut.title: How Arc::get_mut works
get_mut.description: &mut to the value, only when this is the only owner (no Weak either).

slides.caption: A unique Arc can be changed without a Mutex.
For shared mutation across threads, use Arc<Mutex<T>>.

into_inner.title: How Arc::into_inner works
into_inner.description: Gives the value to whichever owner lets go last.

slides.caption: Exactly one of the owners receives Some; the others get None.
The first owner to let go gets None.
The last one gets the value.
Prefer it over try_unwrap when several threads might finish at the same time.

unwrap_or_clone.title: How Arc::unwrap_or_clone works
unwrap_or_clone.description: An owned value: moved out if unique, cloned if shared.

slides.caption: No copy unless another owner still needs the value.
The Rc version works the same.

weak_count.title: How Arc::weak_count works
weak_count.description: How many sync::Weak pointers point at the value.

slides.caption: Weak pointers do not keep the value alive.

upgrade.title: How sync::Weak::upgrade works
upgrade.description: Turns a Weak back into an Arc if the value still exists.

slides.caption: upgrade atomically checks the strong count and, if it is above zero, adds one.
An Arc still owns it: Some.
The last Arc was dropped: None.
Typical for caches and observer lists shared between threads.

from.title: How Arc::from works
from.description: Moves a value (a String, Vec, Box, …) into a new Arc.

slides.caption: Arc<str> is a thread-safe shared string.
The text moves into the Arc.
Cloning an Arc<str> copies only a pointer.

new_cyclic.title: How Arc::new_cyclic works
new_cyclic.description: Creates an Arc whose value holds a Weak pointer to itself.

slides.caption: The closure gets the Weak before the value exists.
The node stores a Weak to itself.
Upgrading it gives the same Arc.

pin.title: How Arc::pin works
pin.description: A pinned value shared across threads: Pin<Arc<T>>.

slides.caption: Clones share the same pinned value.
The value goes into an Arc.
Used for futures shared between tasks.

downcast.title: How Arc<dyn Any>::downcast works
downcast.description: Gets the concrete type back from an Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>.

as_ptr.title: How Arc::as_ptr works
as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the shared value.

slides.caption: Every clone points to the same place.

arc_weak-new.title: How sync::Weak::new works
arc_weak-new.description: An empty thread-safe Weak that points nowhere.

slides.caption: No allocation; upgrade always returns None.
Starting value for a parent pointer.

arc_weak-strong_count.title: How sync::Weak::strong_count works
arc_weak-strong_count.description: How many Arc owners remain, seen from a Weak.

slides.caption: Lets a Weak check whether the value still exists.
upgrade() is the usual way to use it.

arc_weak-weak_count.title: How sync::Weak::weak_count works
arc_weak-weak_count.description: How many Weak pointers exist, seen from a Weak.

slides.caption: Counts the Weak pointers to the allocation.
0 once the last Arc is gone.

arc_weak-ptr_eq.title: How sync::Weak::ptr_eq works
arc_weak-ptr_eq.description: true if two Weak pointers share an allocation.

default.title: How Arc::default works
default.description: A new Arc holding the inner type's default value.

slides.caption: Handy for shared configuration that starts empty.

from_iter.title: How collect into Arc<[T]> works
from_iter.description: Collects an iterator straight into a shared Arc<[T]>.

new_uninit.title: How Arc::new_uninit works
new_uninit.description: Allocates an Arc whose value will be written later.

slides.caption: Write the value while the Arc is still unique.

into_raw.title: How Arc::into_raw works
into_raw.description: Turns an Arc into a raw pointer, keeping the reference count.

title.text: let p = Arc::into_raw(a); let a = unsafe { Arc::from_raw(p) };

slides.caption: Common for callbacks that carry user data through C.
Each into_raw needs exactly one from_raw.

arc_weak-as_ptr.title: How sync::Weak::as_ptr works
arc_weak-as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the value a thread-safe Weak points at.

slides.caption: Useful as a key for identity maps.

from_raw.title: How Arc::from_raw works
from_raw.description: Turns a pointer from Arc::into_raw back into an Arc (unsafe).

increment_strong_count.title: How Arc::increment_strong_count works
increment_strong_count.description: Adds one owner through a raw pointer (unsafe).

decrement_strong_count.title: How Arc::decrement_strong_count works
decrement_strong_count.description: Removes one owner through a raw pointer (unsafe).

assume_init.title: How Arc<MaybeUninit<T>>::assume_init works
assume_init.description: Turns an initialised Arc<MaybeUninit<T>> into Arc<T> (unsafe).

new_zeroed.title: How Arc::new_zeroed works
new_zeroed.description: An Arc with zero-filled memory, as Arc<MaybeUninit<T>>.

new_uninit_slice.title: How Arc::new_uninit_slice works
new_uninit_slice.description: An Arc<[MaybeUninit<T>]> of n elements to fill.

new_zeroed_slice.title: How Arc::new_zeroed_slice works
new_zeroed_slice.description: An Arc slice of n zeroed elements.

arc_weak-into_raw.title: How sync::Weak::into_raw works
arc_weak-into_raw.description: Turns a thread-safe Weak into a raw pointer.

arc_weak-from_raw.title: How sync::Weak::from_raw works
arc_weak-from_raw.description: Turns a pointer from Weak::into_raw back into a Weak (unsafe).
